**Context window.**
Context length varies dramatically across models.
Transformer-based models are typically limited to 512--6,144 tokens due to quadratic attention cost (though ALiBi in DNABERT-2 allows extrapolation beyond the 2,048-token training window).
Sub-quadratic architectures achieve much longer contexts: HyenaDNA reaches 1M nucleotides, Evo reaches 131k nucleotides, and Caduceus was evaluated at up to 131k nucleotides.

Hi-C extends chromosome conformation capture (3C) to an unbiased genome-wide scale.
The protocol involves: (1) crosslinking cells with formaldehyde to fix 3D proximity relationships, (2) restriction enzyme digestion, (3) fill-in of overhangs with biotinylated nucleotides, (4) ligation of spatially proximate fragments, (5) purification of ligated junctions via streptavidin pulldown, and (6) paired-end sequencing.
The resulting read pairs indicate which genomic loci were in spatial proximity at the time of crosslinking.
The authors generated 8.4 million read pairs from human lymphoblastoid cells (GM06990), achieving approximately 1 Mb resolution genome-wide.

The headline result: **3D attention bias produces a statistically significant improvement on RNA SS prediction** (mean +0.010 F1, paired t=3.11, p<0.05, 3/3 seeds positive). The effect is small but real, and it was obtained with the most conservative setup (power law bias, C3' backbone distance with 23% contact recall, DNA-pretrained model on RNA task, 104 training sequences). paragraph: t001 supported this proposition via the empirical decay slope (~0.19/token → calibrates PowerLawBias `p ∈ [-0.5, -0.1]`). t034 partially disputes the *DNA-derived parameterization* when applied to RNA: RNA profiles have the same *shape* but operate over longer effective sequences, so the same decay slope may produce attention modulation that is miscalibrated in magnitude on RNA inputs.

title: RNA Attention Profile Validation (t034) \u2014 Shape Transfers, Scale Does\
paragraph: Layer 6-11 mean R90 on RNA is 27.71 tokens vs 12.35 on DNA@100bp, a **2.24x ratio**. This fails the pre-registered secondary gate of ≤2.0x by 12%. Per-layer R90 deltas peak at layer 7 (37.25 vs 14.58; delta 22.67 tokens).

title: Pilot Results and Experiment Readiness
paragraph: The 23% contact recall reveals a fundamental limitation: C3'-to-C3' distance captures backbone geometry but misses a large fraction of structural contacts. For RNA secondary structure — where base pairing is the prediction target — the relevant proximity is between bases (N1-N1 for purines, N3-N3 for pyrimidines, hydrogen bond donor-acceptor distances of ~2.8-3.0 A), not between backbone C3' atoms. Two nucleotides can be base-paired (structurally close, target label = paired) while their C3' atoms are at moderate distance, especially in non-Watson-Crick pairs.

title: RNA Attention Profile Validation (t034) \u2014 Shape Transfers, Scale Does\
paragraph: Per-layer KL(RNA | DNA@100bp) across all 12 layers is **tiny** (primary cohort layers 6-11 mean = 0.0152, max = 0.0192; all-layer range 0.006–0.028). This is 30–52× below the pre-registered gate of 0.5–1.0. The RNA and DNA@100bp attention-vs-distance distributions are essentially shape-identical — the decay curve DNABERT-2 learned on DNA applies unchanged when fed U→T-converted RNA.

title: Interpretation: Experimental-Distance Pilot (t033) and Oversampling Pilot
paragraph: The t033 Arm 2 result provides the first empirical data evidence that 3D distance-based attention bias improves a structure-sensitive benchmark. The evidence is suggestive rather than strong due to the small test set (N=21), single bias function, and single task. The +0.010 F1 effect is genuine (statistically significant, directionally consistent) but modest.

paragraph: Net movement: **from "proposed + suggestive pilot" to "supported with caveats"**. The core mechanistic claim has rigorous empirical support on at least one task / model / bias function combination. The shortcutting caveat (Q15) is now empirically grounded rather than hypothetical: the controlled A-seq contrast shows that a significant fraction of what looked like "3D helps" is attributable to "any pairwise bias helps". title: Was the t037 N=5 D-pw +0.049 effect inflated by env-shift \xD7 small-N interaction?
paragraph: At N=5, single-seed outliers can drive the mean materially. The 5 t037 D-pw seeds may have happened to land in a favorable region of the seed × env interaction space. Standard sampling theory: at N=5 with sd ~0.025, the standard error of the mean is ~0.011, so a single +0.04 seed can shift the group mean by +0.008. With a +0.049 group mean and the next-best estimate at +0.009, ~+0.040 of the t037 effect would need to be sampling artifact — plausible but not parsimonious without environmental help.

title: t045 Q20 Disambiguator + t046 Env-Shift Verification \u2014 All Mechanisms\
paragraph: D-bins-random-4 vs C Δ=−0.004 < +0.003 → triggers the pre-reg's CAPACITY-MATTERS verdict: "192 params was doing real work in D-bins-random. The original t041 match with D-pw was capacity-driven". This makes the t041 D-bins-random Δ=+0.015 dependent on the specific 192-parameter shuffle pattern. Combined with Finding 1, the effect was something specific to that pattern — not a general property of "more params at layers 6-11".

title: t048 \u2014 The 3D bias is reshaping attention (Q24 resolved)
paragraph: The Q25 inverse-direction probe (t051) becomes more interesting as a baseline measurement — partial-Spearman data from t048 shows pretrained + C-fine-tuned attention does *not* implicitly encode 3D proximity (partial Spearman ≈ 0 to +0.15 in mid-late layers), which means the redundancy explanation is *less* likely than the task-locality-ceiling or downstream-routing explanations.

title: Is the RNA-vs-DNA R90 ratio overshoot a sequence-length confound or a genuine
paragraph: t034 measured DNABERT-2's attention profiles on 141 matched BEACON RNA SS sequences and compared them to the DNA@100bp baseline from t001. Per-layer KL divergence is tiny across all 12 layers (mean 0.0152, max 0.0192 on primary cohort layers 6-11) — the attention *shape* is preserved from DNA to RNA. However, the effective radius R90 ratio is 2.24x on primary (layers 6-11 mean R90 RNA = 27.71 tokens vs DNA = 12.35 tokens), narrowly failing t034's pre-registered ≤2.0x gate and triggering the STOP verdict.
